title: 2005 AMC 12B Problem 20
statement: Let \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) \(d,\) \(e,\) \(f,\) \(g\) and \(h\) be distinct elements in the set \[ \{-7, -5, -3, -2, 2, 4, 6, 13\}. \] What is the minimum possible value of \[ \begin{aligned} &(a + b + c + d)^2 \\ &\quad {}+ (e + f + g + h)^2? \end{aligned} \]

solutions.text:
The elements sum to \(8.\) If \(a + b + c + d = x,\) then \(e + f + g + h = 8 - x,\) so \[ x^2 + (8 - x)^2 = 2(x - 4)^2 + 32. \]

This is minimized when \(x = 4,\) giving \(32.\) But \(13\) must lie in one group, and no three of the remaining elements add with \(13\) to make \(4\) (that would need three of them to sum to \(-9\)). With \(-7,\) the other two would need to sum to \(-2,\) which no available pair does; without \(-7,\) replacing any term in \(-5-3-2=-10\) raises the sum past \(-9.\) So \(x = 4\) is unattainable and \((x - 4)^2 \ge 1.\)

The minimum is \(2(1) + 32 = 34,\) achieved for instance by \(\{-7, -5, 2, 13\}\) (sum \(3\)) and \(\{-3, -2, 4, 6\}\) (sum \(5\)).

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The whole set sums to \(8,\) so if one group sums to \(x,\) the other sums to \(8 - x\)
